descriptionAr: About Us At Cloudflare, we are on a mission to help build a better Internet. Today the company runs one of the world’s largest networks that powers millions of websites and other Internet properties for customers ranging from individual bloggers to SMBs to Fortune 500 companies. Cloudflare protects and accelerates any Internet application online without adding hardware, installing software, or changing a line of code. Internet properties powered by Cloudflare all have web traffic routed through its intelligent global network, which gets smarter with every request. As a result, they see significant improvement in performance and a decrease in spam and other attacks. Cloudflare was named to Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top Company Cultures list and ranked among the World’s Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company. At Cloudflare, we’re not looking for people who wait for a polished roadmap; we’re looking for the builders who see the cracks in the Internet that everyone else has simply learned to live with. We value candidates who have the instinct to spot a "normalized" problem and the AI-native curiosity to create a solution using the latest tools. Our culture is built on iteration, leveraging AI to ship faster today to make it better tomorrow, while ensuring that every improvement, no matter how small, is shared across the team to lift everyone up. If you’re the type of person who values curiosity over bureaucracy, and that AI is a partner in solving tough problems to keep the Internet moving forward, you’ll fit right in. Available Locations: Austin, TX | Lisbon, Portugal | London, UK About the role The Snr Software Engineer, AI & Infrastructure Planning role helps Cloudflare build, deploy, and operate one of the world's largest distributed networks. You will build an auditable multi-agent system on Cloudflare’s platform to replace notebooks and email threads with agent-driven forecasts, supply plans, cost models, and workflow approvals into agent workflows that planners & executives rely on for decision analysis. Responsibilities Collaborate closely with capacity planning, networking, and data center engineering teams to encode technical domain expertise into structured specifications, formal data contracts, and agent functional capabilities. Architect, deploy, and maintain scalable production agents and durable workflows leveraging the Cloudflare Workers ecosystem, including Durable Objects, Workflows, D1, R2, Queues, Vectorize, Workers AI, and AI Gateway. Translate core infrastructure planning functions—such as forecasting, supply planning, cost modeling, narrative documentation, and executive approvals—into automated  LLM deployment or deterministic logic based agent workflows designed for critical decision-making analysis. Implement rigorous risk tiering, formal approval checkpoints, detailed audit logs, and execution lineage to ensure safe autonomous operations. Incorporate predictive statistical and machine learning models into agent systems, establishing robust BigQuery data pipelines, optimized access patterns, and continuous monitoring. Author comprehensive technical specifications and Requests for Comments (RFCs), perform peer design reviews, and establish architectural standards for AI agent deployment across the organization. Desirable Skills, Knowledge, and Experience Senior-level software engineering experience, with security conscious production systems you can point to (repos, releases, services you operated). Strong TypeScript, and comfort building on serverless or edge runtimes (Cloudflare Workers preferred). HTTP APIs, async, queues, performance. Experience with LLMs and agents: tool calling, structured output, multi-step or multi-agent orchestration, prompt and eval iteration. Experience with durable state and workflows (Durable Objects, Cloudflare Workflows, or equivalents such as Templets updraoral or Step Functions). Demonstrated experience in infrastructure planning: capacity planning, forecasting, networking, CDN, cloud or data center capacity, or adjacent work. We will teach you our specific systems. Solid data skills: SQL, a cloud data warehouse (BigQuery preferred), and working knowledge of forecasting and statistical modeling (backtesting, error metrics, knowing when a model is wrong). Clear written communication: specs, RFCs, and explanations that planners and executives can use. Bonus Points A data science or ML background (time series, optimization, predictive modeling) and Python for scientific computing. Experience with Hono, Zod, OpenAPI, and a modern frontend framework (Astro or React). Experience with peering, BGP, ASN and IX data, backbone or transit planning, or colo, power, and procurement planning. Experience with agent frameworks (LangGraph, Autogen, A2A) and knowing what to borrow and what to discard. CI/CD and infrastructure as code (GitLab CI, Terraform). Experience building LLM evaluation frameworks or human-review workflows. Bias for simple, scalable designs. Compensation Compensation may be adjusted depending on work location. For Portugal-based hires: Estimated annual salary of €66,000-€91,000 Equity This role is eligible to participate in Cloudflare’s equity plan. Benefits Cloudflare offers a complete package of benefits and programs to support you and your family.  Our benefits programs can help you pay health care expenses, support caregiving, build capital for the future and make life a little easier and fun!  The below is a description of our benefits for employees in the United States, and benefits may vary for employees based outside the U.S. Health & Welfare Benefits Medical/Rx Insurance Dental Insurance Vision Insurance Flexible Spending Accounts Commuter Spending Accounts Fertility & Family Forming Benefits On-demand mental health support and Employee Assistance Program Global Travel Medical Insurance Financial Benefits Short and Long Term Disability Insurance Life & Accident Insurance 401(k) Retire

We're building one place where your knowledge, projects, meetings, and AI tools live side by side, so work is faster, clearer, and less fragmented. Millions of individuals, small teams, and large companies run their work on Notion. Notinos (our employees) are customer zero in bringing this future of work to life. We care about craft, building things that last, and the belief that great work is still fundamentally human. Our goal isn’t to ship the next feature. Each and every team of Notinos is working to set the standard for how humans work together in the AI era. From building a business’s system of record to making and managing AI agents to automating away the busy work, we care deeply about giving our customers more time for their life’s work. About the Role: This is an opportunity to join Notion's TPM organization as a key partner to our Engineering, Product, and Design (EPD) leadership. You'll work hand-in-hand with the most senior engineering, product, and design leaders at Notion to help run the programs and operating rhythms that keep EPD focused, aligned, and shipping. You'll own a portfolio of programs that spans internal engineering initiatives as well as cross-functional, externally facing efforts with partners across Go-to-Market, Marketing, Support, and beyond, ensuring that we meet the ever-growing expectations of our global user base. This role can be based in either San Francisco or New York City. We work from our offices on Mondays, Tuesdays and Thursdays (our Anchor Days) because we do our best thinking and building together in person. We’re looking for someone who’s excited to work alongside the team during those days. What You'll Achieve: Work closely with senior EPD leaders to drive multiple concurrent programs, from internal engineering initiatives (platform, infrastructure, quality, and developer productivity) to external, cross-functional programs such as major launches and customer-facing commitments Combine long-term vision with near-term execution: be accountable for overall delivery, including prioritization, success criteria, and program communications in coordination with your partners Help design and run EPD's operating cadence, including planning cycles, goal-setting, roadmap reviews, leadership syncs, and business reviews Act as a connector across EPD and the broader company, bringing the right people together, driving decisions to closure, and making sure follow-through happens Prepare clear, concise materials for leadership, including status updates, decision docs, and executive summaries that turn complexity into clarity Monitor program status, proactively identify and communicate issues / risks, and unblock work wherever possible Take on high-priority, ambiguous special projects for EPD leadership and drive them from problem definition to outcome Forge strong partnerships with technical and business leaders across the company, ensuring that team resource investments align with company priorities Skills You'll Need to Bring: 8+ years of technical program management experience at a technology company, or in an equivalent technical or operational capacity, delivering clear and impactful results Proven track record of running multiple complex, cross-functional programs at once, from inception to delivery Enjoy solving hard problems and can turn incomplete, conflicting, or ambiguous inputs into action plans and drive them to impact Strong technical fluency: you can go deep with engineers on systems and tradeoffs, and translate them for non-technical audiences Excellent written and verbal communication, with experience creating executive-ready updates, narratives, and decision docs Strategic thinking and sound judgment: you can see the big picture, prioritize ruthlessly, and know when to escalate Experience designing and running operating rhythms, such as planning, OKRs, leadership meetings, and reviews, for a growing organization Builder mentality and an automation-first instinct: you'd rather script, automate, or build a lightweight tool than run the same process by hand twice, and you bring that bias to every program and operating rhythm you own Notion is committed to providing highly competitive cash compensation, equity, and benefits. The compensation offered for this role will be based on multiple factors such as location, the role’s scope and complexity, and the candidate’s experience and expertise, and may vary from the range provided below. For roles based in San Francisco or New York City, the estimated base salary range for this role is $200,000 - $270,000 per year. descriptionAr: Grafana Labs is the company behind Grafana Cloud, the fully managed observability platform trusted by more than 10,000 organizations to ensure reliability, resolve incidents faster, and optimize telemetry at scale. Built on open source and open standards and designed for interoperability across any stack, Grafana Cloud brings AI to observability and observability to AI, giving teams (and their agents) unified visibility so they can see, understand, and act on all their disparate data, wherever it lives, and move at the speed of their ambitions. Customers, including Anthropic, Bloomberg, NVIDIA, Microsoft, and Salesforce, rely on Grafana Labs. We are a 100% remote company with team members across 40+ countries, backed by leading investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners, Sequoia Capital, GIC, Coatue, J.P. Morgan, CapitalG, and Lead Edge Capital. Learn more at grafana.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X . We’re scaling fast and staying true to what makes us different: an open-source legacy, a global collaborative culture, and a passion for meaningful work. Our team thrives in an innovation-driven environment where transparency, autonomy, and trust fuel everything we do. You may not meet every requirement, and that’s okay. If this role excites you, we’d love you to raise your hand for what could be a truly career-defining opportunity. You will partner closely with our Talent Team to develop a deep understanding of our hiring needs, challenges, organizational structure, and individual team dynamics. In this role, you will own full-cycle recruitment—from sourcing and engaging passive and active talent globally, to guiding candidates through our end-to-end hiring process, to generating offers and transitioning new hires to our People Ops Specialist for onboarding. You will act as a key internal stakeholder, collaborating across teams to manage headcount reconciliation, oversee compensation alignment and equity, and coordinate and participate in internal interviews. You will also be responsible for ensuring recruitment projects are delivered on time and that all milestones and deliverables are met. This role requires exceptional administrative strength , including the ability to navigate multiple documents and systems while adhering to structured, process-driven workflows. What you'll be doing: Own and execute the Greenhouse recruiting process end-to-end, managing roles from opening through close while ensuring full process adherence. Maintain accurate, complete, and up-to-date hiring documentation , tracking all candidate and hire data to support seamless reporting, audits, and data-driven decision-making. Demonstrate exceptional organizational skills , effectively managing multiple roles, priorities, and deadlines while maintaining attention to detail throughout the day. Provide timely, clear, and proactive updates to hiring managers and business stakeholders, anticipating needs and addressing issues before they arise. Operate with a proactive mindset, staying one step ahead of recruiting workflows to prevent bottlenecks and ensure a smooth, efficient hiring experience. Sourcing is a primary part of your role. You are confident in engaging passive candidates and utilizing the team’s networks to engage with candidates appropriately. What makes you a great fit: 5+ Years recruiting experience working with senior leaders in SaaS/Tech space. Work in a remote-first company where communication is key . You’re comfortable in a  high-paced  environment. You embrace change and ambiguity. You’re familiar with Greenhouse and  LinkedIn Recruiter. Compensation & Rewards: In the United States, the Base compensation range for this role is USD $144,000 - $160,000. Actual compensation may vary based on level, experience, and skillset as assessed in the interview process. Benefits include equity, bonus (if applicable), and other benefits listed  here . All of our roles include Restricted Stock Units (RSUs), giving every team member ownership in Grafana Labs' success. We believe in shared outcomes—RSUs help us stay aligned and invested as we scale globally. *Compensation ranges are country specific. If you are applying for this role from a different location than listed above, your recruiter will discuss your specific market’s defined pay range & benefits at the beginning of the process. Why You’ll Thrive at Grafana Labs: 100% Remote, Global Culture -  As a remote-only company, we bring together talent from around the world, united by a culture of collaboration and shared purpose. Scaling Organization – Tackle meaningful work in a high-growth, ever-evolving environment. Transparent Communication – Expect open decision-making and regular company-wide updates. Innovation-Driven – Autonomy and support to ship great work and try new things. Open Source Roots – Built on community-driven values that shape how we work. Empowered Teams – High trust, low ego culture that values outcomes over optics. Career Growth Pathways – Defined opportunities to grow and develop your career. descriptionAr: About Sentry Software runs the world and the pace is faster than ever. Sentry helps developers fix errors and performance issues before users notice, so teams can spend less time firefighting and more time building. Trusted by 200,000+ organizations, Sentry is today’s application monitoring standard and our team is building its AI-native future. About the role You’ll join the team behind Sentry’s Size Analysis and Snapshots, two products that check every pull request before it ships. Size Analysis breaks down iOS and Android builds to explain why an app got bigger. Snapshots catches unintended visual changes by diffing screenshots against a baseline. Both run in our customers’ CI, report straight to Source Code Management providers, and handle some of the heaviest payloads at Sentry: multi-GB app binaries and builds with tens of thousands of images. In this role you will You’ll work full-stack with a backend lean, owning features from the moment a build arrives from CI, to the moment when UI engineers use that data to decide whether to merge. You’ll own the codebase behind our mobile binary analysis and large-scale image comparison. You’ll share the pipeline, the GitHub integration and on-call with the rest of the Sentry team. Build and tune the backend services and task-based pipelines that ingest, analyze and compare builds, with large artifacts in object storage, fast and reliable on multi-GB binaries and changesets with tens of thousands of screenshots Extend our product: own the functionality end-to-end, react on feedback and come up with proposals for further product development. Own the GitHub integration end to end: PR status checks, comments, approvals and webhooks, including races, duplicates and missing-baseline edge cases Ship frontend features such as treemaps, build comparisons and diff viewers that stay fast on huge datasets Run what you build: deploys across regions, metrics, logging and on-call, and be the person who debugs the weird customer build You’ll love this job if you Want your work to show up in the pull requests our customers open every day, not buried in a dashboard nobody checks Like problems with real weight: a multi-GB IPA, tens of thousands of screenshots in a single build, a binary format with sparse documentation Would rather own a feature from upload to UI than hand off half of it (end-to-end ownership) Enjoy building for developers, who will tell you exactly what’s wrong and why Want to help two products that started at a startup grow into core parts of Sentry Qualifications 3+ years building production web services, with strong Python (Django preferred) and a habit of typed, tested code Working proficiency in React and TypeScript, enough to ship a full feature without handing off the frontend Experience with async task systems and event pipelines (Kafka, task queues, worker pools), including idempotency, locking, retries and their failure modes Experience with Postgres schema design and migrations that work under rolling deploys, plus pragmatic rollout habits like feature flags and revertable changes A track record of performance work: profiling, parallelism, memory reduction and large-file streaming through object storage Bonus points for: Hands-on experience with mobile build artifacts and tooling (LIEF, bundletool, apksigner, link maps, DWARF, code signing) Image processing or pixel-diff tooling GitHub Apps or the Checks API Data visualization, especially treemaps Prior work on developer tools, CI or observability products We are obliged by law to quote the minimum wage of EUR 60,844,-- gross per year for this position, in accordance with the respective collective agreement (IT-KV). The salary that Sentry offers you is adjusted to the current market situation and will be above the IT-KV. A successful candidate will be eligible to participate in Sentry’s employee benefit plans/programs applicable to the candidate’s position (including incentive compensation, equity grants, paid time off, and group health insurance coverage). See Sentry Benefits for more details about the Company’s benefit plans/programs. Equal Opportunity at Sentry Sentry is committed to providing equal employment opportunities to its employees and candidates for employment regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender identity, veteran status, or other legally-protected characteristic. This commitment includes the provision of reasonable accommodations to employees and candidates for employment with physical or mental disabilities who require such accommodations in order to (a) perform the essential functions of their jobs, or (b) seek employment with Sentry. We strive to build a diverse team, with an inclusive culture where every teammate can thrive. Sentry is an open-source company because we believe that everyone, everywhere, should have the ability and tools to make great software. Software should be accessible. That starts with making our industry accessible. If you need assistance or an accommodation due to a disability, you may contact us at accommodations@sentry.io . Want to learn more about how Sentry handles applicant data? Get the details in our Applicant Privacy Policy .

descriptionAr: At Linear, we're building the product development system for teams and agents. AI is fundamentally changing how software gets built, and we’re shaping the tools this new era requires. Founded in 2019, Linear has become the platform of choice for more than 50,000 companies (including OpenAI, Coinbase, and Ramp) to plan, build, and ship their products. Today, our team is distributed across North America, Europe, and Australia, and we’re continuing to grow internationally. What unites us is relentless focus, fast execution, and a deep care for software craftsmanship. Over the past few years, Linear has experienced incredible organic growth and has become the default tool of choice for many of the world’s best product teams. We are now layering a product-led sales motion on top of our existing self-serve business to further accelerate our ambitions and bring the magic of Linear to even more and larger companies. As an Account Executive at Linear, you’ll contribute to the future of our product and help high-impact companies build better software. Location & work mode While Linear is a remote-first company across the US and Europe, this role is specifically based in London. We’re looking for someone who can work from our London office in Shoreditch 3 days per week (Mondays, Tuesdays, Thursdays), as this role will be closely connected to in-person collaboration with our growing sales presence in the region. What you'll do Become a product expert and help customers use Linear effectively; assist prospects through the trial and evaluation phase Generate a strong pipeline and exceed quarterly and annual targets Build relationships with key stakeholders within accounts Stay up to date with our product offering, industry trends, competitive landscape, and market trends to continuously adapt sales strategies and approaches for maximum impact Be the voice of the customer; advocate for customers by surfacing product or adoption blockers to our product team What we're looking for 5+ years in a quota-carrying sales role Experience selling to a technical audience; bonus if you have previous experience working with a collaboration or developer tool SaaS and startup experience; comfortable working and adapting in a fast-paced and flexible environment Strong written and verbal communication, presentation, and product demonstration skills Highly autonomous with a bias for action. Owner’s mindset to quickly come up to speed on product, market, ICP, and unique differentiators What we offer We're a small, focused team that cares deeply about the quality of our work and the people we do it with. Here's what you can expect: Competitive salary and equity Employee-friendly equity terms Daily meal and coffee stipend on every workday Health coverage (based on country requirements) 5 weeks paid vacation, plus local statutory holidays 4 months paid parental leave Paid month off after 4 years & every 2 years thereafter Regular team events and off-sites Learn how we think and work A story about our mission: Read Me Our hiring process: How we hire at Linear How we work: Designing remote work at Linear Our CEO and co-founder, Karri at 20VC: How to Grow Capital Efficiently in a World of BS Growth Make an Org Chart You Want to Ship — Advice from Linear on How Heirloom Tomatoes Should Inspire Team Design Building our teams: Why and how we do work trials at Linear A video series: Conversations on Quality Read about our recent Series C Fundraise and Giving our team liquidity A note on recruitment fraud: all official Linear hiring communication comes from an @ linear.app email address, and all open roles are listed at linear.app/careers . We never ask candidates for payment or financial information. Suspicious messages can be reported to security@linear.app . Linear is an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate based on race, color, religion, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic under applicable law.

Cloudflare protects and accelerates any Internet application online without adding hardware, installing software, or changing a line of code. Internet properties powered by Cloudflare all have web traffic routed through its intelligent global network, which gets smarter with every request. As a result, they see significant improvement in performance and a decrease in spam and other attacks. Cloudflare was named to Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top Company Cultures list and ranked among the World’s Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company. At Cloudflare, we’re not looking for people who wait for a polished roadmap; we’re looking for the builders who see the cracks in the Internet that everyone else has simply learned to live with. We value candidates who have the instinct to spot a "normalized" problem and the AI-native curiosity to create a solution using the latest tools. Our culture is built on iteration, leveraging AI to ship faster today to make it better tomorrow, while ensuring that every improvement, no matter how small, is shared across the team to lift everyone up. If you’re the type of person who values curiosity over bureaucracy, and that AI is a partner in solving tough problems to keep the Internet moving forward, you’ll fit right in. Available Locations: Atlanta, GA; Austin, TX; Denver, CO; New York City; San Francisco, CA; Seattle, WA; Washington D.C.; Toronto, Canada About the role Many of Cloudflare’s critical internal services run on Kubernetes. These services include those responsible for Cloudflare’s control plane and APIs, data analytics and other internal tools used to manage our global network. These Kubernetes platforms are purpose-built from the ground up and run on bare metal Linux in different regions around the world. The scale we work at involves tens of thousands of containers and terabits per second of network traffic. The team takes pride in knowing this platform helps run parts of the global Internet. As an engineer on the Kubernetes platform team, you'll be building the tools to help engineers deploy and operate the services that make Cloudflare work. Our mission is to provide a reliable and flexible platform to help product teams release new software efficiently and safely. The role includes both software engineering and DevOps operational responsibilities. Responsibilities Design scalable and resilient systems that can keep up with company growth. Work with application teams to understand their needs and challenges, and help them choose the best way to architect their systems to run well in our Kubernetes environment. Harden the platform against security threats, noisy neighbours, and accidents. Improve the efficiency of our use of resources such as CPU, memory, bandwidth, and storage. Help respond to, resolve, and prevent incidents impacting the platform or our users. Contribute back to the open source community. Some of our favorite open source projects include: Envoy, Contour, Consul, etcd, cdk8s, Cloudprober, Calico, Ceph, Rook, KubeVirt, and more. Desirable Skills, Knowledge, and Experience Experience managing production Kubernetes clusters. Experience operating systems on-premise at scale in roles such as SRE, systems design or architecture. Excellent debugging skills in a Linux environment. Knowledge of how container runtimes work inside of Linux (isolation, storage, and networking). A firm grasp of IP networking including routing and iptables/nftables. Ability to work with codebases in Go, TypeScript, and Bash/shell. The ability to break down complex problems into smaller pieces, provide options, talk through trade-offs, build consensus, and drive the effort to solve the problem. Bonus Points Familiarity with building platforms across multiple zones and regions as the foundation for other teams to build distributed highly-available applications. Experience with configuration management frameworks such as SaltStack or Ansible. Experience with continuous deployment tooling like ArgoCD and Argo Rollouts. Operational/administrator experience with etcd, Ceph, Rook, KubeVirt, CNIs, ClusterAPI, Envoy, and/or Contour. Experience as a user of Prometheus, Elasticsearch/Kibana, Vault, Redis, and/or Consul. Compensation Compensation may be adjusted depending on work location. For San Francisco based hires: Estimated annual salary of $194,000 - $266,000 For Denver based hires: Estimated annual salary of $168,000 - $231,000 For New York City based hires: Estimated annual salary of $185,000 - $254,000 For Seattle based hires: Estimated annual salary of $185,000 - $254,000 For Washington D.C. based hires: Estimated annual salary of $185,000 - $254,000 For Toronto, Canada based hires: Estimated annual salary of $150,000 - $206,000 Applications will be accepted until December 25, 2026. Equity This role is eligible to participate in Cloudflare's equity plan. Benefits Cloudflare offers a complete package of benefits and programs to support you and your family. Our benefits programs can help you pay health care expenses, support caregiving, build capital for the future and make life a little easier and fun! descriptionAr: About Ramp Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books. The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving. We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome. The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same. If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it. About the Role Ramp builds software that moves real money, from bill payments and corporate cards to reimbursements, accounting integrations, and travel. Our customers rely on us to keep their operations running: invoices get paid, books get closed, and finance leaders can trust the data behind every decision. In this role, you will be the person who spots where customers are getting stuck and drives issues to a clear resolution. You will learn a complex product deeply enough to troubleshoot across payments, bank linking, accounting syncs, and card programs, then partner with teams across Engineering, Risk, Product, and Partnerships to get problems solved. This is not script-based support. You will triage, investigate, and make high-signal judgment calls throughout the day. You will thrive in this role if you are a systems thinker and deeply customer obsessed. Support is the baseline. How you think about improving processes, tools, and outcomes is what sets you apart. What You’ll Do Be the voice of Ramp's Customer Support. You'll spend your day engaging with customers, primarily via live calls, email, and chat. Diagnose across a broad product surface. Ramp isn't one product — it's payments, cards, travel, accounting integrations, and more. You'll need to understand how they connect and where they break. Operate with an ownership mindset, managing escalations end-to-end. You take full accountability for every ticket you handle. When an issue crosses team boundaries — risk, engineering, product, partnerships — you route it correctly, follow up, and make sure the customer isn't left waiting. You'll work across Zendesk, internal tooling, and Slack-based escalation workflows. Build and shape AI tools, not just use them. Ramp is building AI into CX operations. You'll use AI-powered research tools and proprietary tools like Glass daily, provide direct feedback on what's working, and play an active role in how these tools evolve. You're not just a user — you're a builder. We are all builders at Ramp. Ship improvements, not just flag them. When you notice a process gap, a missing SOP, or a knowledge base article that's sending associates down the wrong path, you don't just raise it — you have the autonomy to roll up your sleeves and fix it. Leverage AI to solve problems, build automations, and improve the systems around you. The best people in this role make the whole team better. Communicate with precision and empathy. Our customers are financially sophisticated. You need to explain what's happening, what you're doing about it, and what they should expect — clearly and without filler. What You Need You're a systems thinker: you don't just solve the ticket in front of you, you ask why the problem exists and how to prevent it from happening again. You actively use AI tools — Claude, Notion AI, research and workflow tools — and can demonstrate how you've applied them to get real work done. This is a hard requirement. You're fast-moving while holding yourself to a high bar for execution: you balance speed, accuracy, and thoroughness in every interaction. You can hold a technical conversation about how systems connect (APIs, bank integrations, accounting software) even if you're not writing code. You manage competing priorities without dropping things. When you have 15 open issues across 4 internal teams, nothing falls through. You write clearly and concisely. You can explain a payment reconciliation issue to a CFO without jargon. You're comfortable on the phone. Many interactions start there. You have a demonstrated track record of exceeding key performance standards, including CSAT, QA, and speed-of-service metrics. Nice to Haves Experience building workflows or automations using AI tools, not just prompting Familiarity with accounting workflows (AP/AR, GL, reconciliation) or ERP integrations (NetSuite, QuickBooks, Sage) Background in payments infrastructure (ACH, wire transfers, card networks) Track record of working somewhere that shipped product fast and expected CX to keep up Why be a CX Associate at Ramp Cross-functional exposure from day one. You work directly with Product, Engineering, and GTM teams — not siloed into a support queue. AI tools and unlimited access. Unlimited tokens, proprietary AI tools like Glass, and a culture that expects you to use them to move faster and build smarter. Career growth that you own. Grow within CX, explore other functions internally, or carve out a path that doesn't exist yet. If you're invested, we're invested. Culture that's different from a call center. Team events, in-person offsites, and a genuine commitment to building a team people want to be part of. descriptionAr: Who are we? Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company. We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems. We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that. We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft. We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us! Why this team? Internal Infrastructure builds the infrastructure and tools used to train, evaluate, and serve Cohere's foundation models. You will work with AI researchers and ML engineers on stability, scalability, and observability. The work accelerates the models behind Cohere's platform, North. You will own the developer platform researchers use to write, build, and debug training code: dev environments, container images, CI, and training instrumentation. The role includes a compensated 24x7 on-call rotation. What you will do Run secure developer environments that stay controlled and accelerate developer velocity as the research org scales. Own container image build and CI/CD tooling. Instrument training code and build self-service tooling so researchers can see why a run failed and debug it themselves. Set infrastructure best practices through AI enablement, documentation, and office hours. Troubleshoot production failures and performance problems, and leave the system easier to operate than you found it. Build automation, infrastructure-as-code, and observability so the platform stays maintainable. We hire at more than one level. We set level based on the scope you've owned and how independently you drive work. You may be a good fit if you have Run a developer platform in production: CI, image builds, dev environments, or internal tooling that many engineers depend on. Made ML engineers or researchers faster without making the platform fragile. Enough Linux and Kubernetes to debug production systems. Experience operating a GPU cluster is a plus. Written software in Python or Go. You would rather extend a solid open-source project than rebuild it. Worked with researchers, ML engineers, or another team whose goals were not identical to yours. Found a bottleneck, proposed a fix, and driven it in a fast-moving environment. If this does not line up exactly with your experience, we still encourage you to apply. Full-Time Employees at Cohere enjoy these Perks: A weekly lunch stipend of $75/£75 or equivalent in your local currency for lunch. Full health and dental benefits, including a separate budget for mental health. RRSP matching, 401K, Pension Scheme. 100% Parental Leave top-up for up to 6 months, for either parent. Annual enrichment benefits: Arts & culture, fitness/wellness, quality time, and a workspace improvement credit. Education & learning stipend for conferences, courses, and coaching. 6 weeks of paid vacation (30 working days!) Budget for traveling to other offices if you are remote, plus an annual company offsite. How and Where We Work: Cohere is remote-friendly, but we also have offices in Toronto, London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul with more opening soon. For those in the office: a daily lunch program, plenty of snacks, and regular community and social events. We launched out of Y Combinator's W20 cohort . We are: Product-led . More than 500K organizations have installed PostHog, mostly driven by word-of-mouth. We have intensely strong product-market fit. Default alive . Revenue is growing incredibly quickly, and we're very efficient. We raise money to push ambition and grow faster, not to keep the lights on. Well-funded. We've raised more than $180m from some of the world's top investors. We're set up for a long, ambitious journey. We're focused on building an awesome product for end users, hiring exceptional teammates, shipping fast, and being as weird as possible . Things we care about Transparency: Everyone can read about our roadmap, how we pay (or even let go of) people, our strategy, and how we work, in our public company handbook . Internally, we share revenue, notes and slides from board meetings, and fundraising plans, so everyone has the context they need to make good decisions. Autonomy: We don’t tell anyone what to do. Everyone chooses what to work on next based on what's going to have the biggest impact on our customers, and what they find interesting and motivating to work on. Engineers lead product teams and make product decisions . Teams are flexible and easy to change when needed. Shipping fast: Why not now? We want to build a lot of products; we can't do that shipping at a normal pace. We've built the company around small teams – autonomous, highly-efficient groups of cracked engineers who can outship much larger companies because they own their products end-to-end. Time for building: Nothing gets shipped in a meeting. We're a natively remote company. We default to async communication – PRs > Issues > Slack. Tuesdays and Thursdays are meeting-free days , and we prioritize heads down building time over perfect coordination. This will be the most productive job you've ever had. Being weird: Weird means redesigning an already world-class website for the 5th time. It means shipping literally every product that relates to customer data. It means building an objectively unnecessary developer toy with dubious shareholder value. Doing weird stuff is a competitive advantage. And it's fun. Who we're looking for We're hiring for a range of roles here. What you end up working on will depend on your exact skillset and preferences, so choose your own adventure. In general we seek Product Engineers who are: Enthusiastic drivers. We need proactive people that can fully own projects and get them done, and know to get help when needed. This is what being a product engineer is all about. "Are we there yet?" is the wrong question. Optimistic problem solvers. Things get hard here sometimes – whether it's scaling, shipping complex products, handling a stream of support requests, or trying to ship something that touches multiple teams. We need people who won't get disheartened, and will collaborate, iterate, and ship their way out of anything. Grown ups. We’re an international bunch of weirdos, but one thing unites us: everyone is kind, considerate, and professional towards each other. This isn't about age or experience , it's about being low-ego, flexible, and respectful. Genuine builders. PostHog is full of people who just love building stuff, people who would still be building software even if there wasn't a paycheck at the end. If this sounds like you, we should talk. What you'll be doing Owning products and features from beginning to end. This means originating ideas based on your intuition, talking to users, and understanding our strategy and goals. It means testing MVPs in production with real users. It means iterating on their feedback , owning pricing, and ensuring the ongoing success of your work. Collaborating with design (when necessary). Product engineers at PostHog are full stack, so we expect you to ship and own the basic UX of your work using our design system . From there, it's up to you to decide when to collaborate with our design team to iterate and polish the experience. Talking to users. Good product engineers read feedback from users and iterate quickly. Great product engineers have users they're friendly with, talk with them frequently, bounce ideas off them, and iterate with them when they ship new things. Doing support. Every week, one person in each engineering team is designated the Support hero . Their job is to investigate and resolve issues reported by customers for their product. Giving users support from real engineers, and shipping fixes and improvements in real-time, is one of the best ways to spark joy in users. This role will also include some on-call time , too. Writing docs. We have a content team that will collaborate with you on reviewing, polishing, and improving your documentation, but the best person to document a new feature is the person who built it. Requirements You've built things agents actually use. More and more of what we ship is used by agents, not people, and building for them is genuinely different. We want someone who's done it and has the scars: an API an agent can drive, an MCP server, evals, docs written for a machine. Side projects count. Full-stack experience with relevant technologies – e.g. Python or similar, React or similar, something to do with big data is a bonus. Experience taking a project from 0 to 1. You might have led a project, been a founder previously, or built an impressive side project. Strong writing skills. We document everythi

If you can't solve something, you find who can and make the connection. ❌ You also won't be pasting AI answers back to customers. We use AI every day, but we expect you to test things out for yourself and write a reply to the customer that's better than the one it would write. Here's more on how we think about that . How we work You'll be the face of PostHog for many of our customers. Most of them are engineers, so they want help from someone who understands the technical detail and writes back like a person. We want support to be part of why people choose PostHog. We provide support across EU and US time zones, and we're hiring in both. We work in public by default, so you'll ask for help, share what you learn, and discuss problems in team channels rather than DMs. Read more about how the support team works and our company values . Requirements Experience in at least two programming languages, whether from a previous role, side projects, or something else Experience debugging unfamiliar code or systems, and checking your fix works Clear, concise writing that explains a complex fix without burying the customer in options Thorough investigations that don't slow down your reply to the customer Good at prioritizing and context switching across a busy queue that spans many products Nice to have Experience supporting similar products, e.g. analytics, session replay, feature flags, experiments, or LLM observability A background in support, teaching, product, or another role where you explain technical things to people If you have a disability, please let us know if there's any way we can make the interview process better for you - we're happy to accommodate! #LI-DNI

We work closely with the OpenTelemetry SIGs to make OpenTelemetry SDKs and instrumentation libraries a success. Members of this team are experts in at least one programming language and have a broad knowledge of various other programming languages. In this role, you will focus on a language-specific implementation of OpenTelemetry in Python , with an emphasis on OpenTelemetry for Generative AI . You will get to work in an upstream-first approach, helping accelerate the OpenTelemetry project while bringing the innovations to Grafana labs products and offerings.  As a company we are remote-first and global, we embrace people of different experiences and backgrounds to build diverse teams where every person brings a unique perspective to the software. We are looking for Engineers that are passionate about communicating with data and providing seamless experiences for our customers to join our growing team! This is a hands-on role for someone with deep Python expertise and an interest in AI. Collaborate in open-source communities. You will develop and maintain the OpenTelemetry Python SDK and instrumentation libraries, working with maintainers and other vendors on specifications, APIs, and implementation decisions. Build Python instrumentation for AI agents. Build instrumentation that connects agent runs, model calls, and tool execution, including across asynchronous code. Contribute to evolving OpenTelemetry conventions for generative AI, with care for sensitive data and metric cardinality. Improve Python SDK performance. Use profiling and benchmarks to evaluate implementation approaches with the upstream community. Make sound tradeoffs around runtime overhead, compatibility, and maintainability. Be visible as an OpenTelemetry expert. Teach others, promote best practices around OpenTelemetry, semantic conventions, and various technologies and frameworks. Both within Grafana Labs and in the broader OpenTelemetry community. Support the technical direction and vision of the team, and contribute to business conversations on the OpenTelemetry strategy at Grafana Labs. Own projects from an ambiguous problem through design, implementation, testing, documentation, and release. Partner in an open and respectful way. Lend your knowledge and skills to our GTM, Product and Support teams. Join customer conversations, investigate instrumentation issues, and turn what you learn into fixes and practical guidance. descriptionAr: Who are we? Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company. We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems. We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that. We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft. We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us! Why this team? Internal Infrastructure builds the infrastructure and tools used to train, evaluate, and serve Cohere's foundation models. You will work with AI researchers and ML engineers on stability, scalability, and observability. The work accelerates the models behind Cohere's platform, North. You will run the shared Kubernetes fleets those workloads land on: multi-cloud GPU and TPU clusters, node health, performance, and the partnership with cloud providers and hardware vendors. The role includes a compensated 24x7 on-call rotation. What you will do Deploy and operate GPU Kubernetes clusters across clouds, and bring up new hardware generations and providers. Work with cloud providers and hardware partners on reliability, performance, and cost, including RDMA and high-speed interconnects. Automate node, GPU, and fabric fault detection and remediation so most faults are fixed without a human. Improve fleet utilization, track cost, and cut the time it takes to get a faulty node back into service. Troubleshoot production failures and performance problems, and leave the system easier to operate than you found it. We hire at more than one level. We set level based on the scope you've owned and how independently you drive work. You may be a good fit if you have Run GPU Kubernetes clusters with thousands of GPUs for ML or HPC workloads. Debugged Linux, networking, and performance problems. Familiarity with RDMA, NCCL, or accelerator health is a plus. Written software in Python or Go. You would rather extend a solid open-source project than rebuild it. Worked with researchers, ML engineers, or another team whose goals were not identical to yours. Found a bottleneck, proposed a fix, and driven it in a fast-moving environment. If this does not line up exactly with your experience, we still encourage you to apply. Full-Time Employees at Cohere enjoy these Perks: A weekly lunch stipend of $75/£75 or equivalent in your local currency for lunch. descriptionAr: Grafana Labs is the company behind Grafana Cloud, the fully managed observability platform trusted by more than 10,000 organizations to ensure reliability, resolve incidents faster, and optimize telemetry at scale. Built on open source and open standards and designed for interoperability across any stack, Grafana Cloud brings AI to observability and observability to AI, giving teams (and their agents) unified visibility so they can see, understand, and act on all their disparate data, wherever it lives, and move at the speed of their ambitions. Customers, including Anthropic, Bloomberg, NVIDIA, Microsoft, and Salesforce, rely on Grafana Labs. We are a 100% remote company with team members across 40+ countries, backed by leading investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners, Sequoia Capital, GIC, Coatue, J.P. Morgan, CapitalG, and Lead Edge Capital. Learn more at grafana.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X . We’re scaling fast and staying true to what makes us different: an open-source legacy, a global collaborative culture, and a passion for meaningful work. Our team thrives in an innovation-driven environment where transparency, autonomy, and trust fuel everything we do. You may not meet every requirement, and that’s okay. If this role excites you, we’d love you to raise your hand for what could be a truly career-defining opportunity. This is a remote opportunity and we would be interested in applications from the UK, Ireland, Spain and Germany. About Grafana Cloud Observability Grafana Cloud is our fully managed observability platform that integrates metrics, logs, and traces with Grafana. It allows our customers to use the best open source observability software, including Prometheus, Mimir, Loki, and Tempo, without the overhead of installing, maintaining and scaling their own observability stack. Within the Observability department, we build products that help customers understand and troubleshoot their applications and infrastructure. We work closely with product management, design and other engineering squads to provide seamless and highly curated experiences for our customers. The squad: Database Observability We build and evolve Grafana Cloud Database Observability. We want to help users understand the health and performance of their databases, identify slow queries and troubleshoot issues through clear, actionable insights. As a frontend engineer on the squad, you’ll build experiences that make complex database telemetry easy to explore and understand. You’ll work closely with backend engineers, product management and design to take ideas from early exploration through to production and improve them based on customer feedback. Our frontend stack is primarily TypeScript and React, interacting with backends written in Go. Your primary focus will be frontend engineering, with opportunities to work across the stack, contributing to APIs and backend functionality to deliver complete customer experiences. Frontend engineers at Grafana also have opportunities to contribute to open source communities. The opportunity: Own technical projects from problem framing through rollout, including getting user feedback and measuring whether what you shipped actually worked. Collaborate with Product Management, Product Design and backend engineers to build intuitive user experiences using clean, reusable components, contributing to supporting APIs and backend functionality where needed. Mentor and collaborate with other engineers. Raise the engineering bar through code review, design feedback, pairing on hard problems, and writing that leaves the team better than you found it. Participate in on-call for the software you help build, contributing to incident response and learning from incidents. Provide technical support in customer escalations and help us identify areas of high friction to address. Collaborate with other squads on shared dependencies, contribute to design proposals, and share the team’s work through demos and technical discussions. We invest heavily in developer productivity. You can use modern AI coding assistants as part of your daily workflow (your choice of tools, within security guidelines), backed by a company-funded usage budget so you can iterate quickly without unnecessary friction. We encourage pragmatic AI-assisted development: faster prototyping, test generation, refactors, documentation, and incident follow-ups, always with strong code review and quality standards. You'll also have access to the latest frontier models from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google. What makes you a great fit: We highly value those who are intellectually curious , who default to transparency , possess a high bias towards action , and who are also kind and enjoy working as a team . Strong frontend engineering experience, with experience across the stack. You have experience building and maintaining production web applications with React and TypeScript, and are comfortable contributing to backend services and APIs. You value maintainability, readability, automated testing and secure development practices. Technical ownership. You have solid experience delivering complex projects, mentoring other engineers and helping teammates work more effectively. You communicate clearly in a fully remote, asynchronous environment. You take responsibility for operating the software you have built . You have experience being on-call, supporting software in production, ensuring reliability and responding to incidents as needed. You enjoy working on complex solutions , building production software systems. You’re a self-starter, capable of tackling complex engineering problems with minimal supervision. User focus and pragmatism. You break complex problems into short feedback loops: analyze, design, deliver an MVP, learn, iterate. AI experience with a practical mindset. You use AI coding tools thoughtfully to improve productivity and quality, validate their output, and share useful practices with teammates. You care

descriptionAr: About the Team We are hiring a Product Partnerships Manager based in Germany with primary responsibility for Germany. You will own some of OpenAI’s most important business development and partnerships in the German market while contributing to broader EMEA and international priorities. The role is responsible for identifying, developing, and executing partnership strategies that accelerate adoption of OpenAI’s products across enterprise, developer, and consumer channels. About the Role You will identify and manage relationships with strategic product partners in Germany and on cross-border opportunities, ranging from global technology platforms to regional champions, including enterprise software vendors, telcos, cloud providers, and government-aligned organizations. This is a deeply cross-functional role requiring close collaboration with Product, Engineering, GTM, Legal, and Policy teams. Although the role has clear accountability for Germany, team priorities may evolve, so you must be ready to take on other markets, verticals, or partnership types. Please note that this role is based out of our Munich office, with 3 days a week required in the office. In this role, you will: Own product partnership strategy and execution for Germany, driving end-to-end partnership sourcing and delivery in the market while contributing to broader EMEA and international priorities. Negotiate and close strategic local and cross-border deals across commercial terms, product scope, data/privacy, brand/marketing, incentives, and expansion paths. Over time, lead senior partner relationships: build trust, align on joint value props, and manage complexity. Partner closely with Product, Engineering, GTM, Legal, Policy, and regional counterparts to align roadmaps, navigate constraints, and execute partnership initiatives. Bring deep knowledge of Germany and a strong point of view on country and sub-region differences across EMEA, informing prioritization, positioning, and partner selection. Apply that judgment flexibly when supporting opportunities beyond Germany or in new verticals. Define success metrics and use analytical judgment to assess progress, surface risks, and communicate outcomes to internal stakeholders. You might thrive in this role if you have: 10+ years of experience in product partnerships or partnership business development within the technology industry. Fluency in English and German. Demonstrated success leading high-impact local and international partnerships involving major technology partners, including complex cross-border work. Deep understanding of the German market, combined with experience operating across multiple countries and international markets. Product-savvy with the ability to engage technical stakeholders credibly and influence product direction and roadmap tradeoffs. Exceptional communication, negotiation, and executive presence. Strong analytical instincts and comfort using data to inform decisions and communicate impact. Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, highly ambiguous environment, operate both independently and collaboratively, and adapt quickly across changing markets, verticals, and partnership types. descriptionAr: About Us At Cloudflare, we are on a mission to help build a better Internet. Today the company runs one of the world’s largest networks that powers millions of websites and other Internet properties for customers ranging from individual bloggers to SMBs to Fortune 500 companies. Cloudflare protects and accelerates any Internet application online without adding hardware, installing software, or changing a line of code. Internet properties powered by Cloudflare all have web traffic routed through its intelligent global network, which gets smarter with every request. As a result, they see significant improvement in performance and a decrease in spam and other attacks. Cloudflare was named to Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top Company Cultures list and ranked among the World’s Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company. At Cloudflare, we’re not looking for people who wait for a polished roadmap; we’re looking for the builders who see the cracks in the Internet that everyone else has simply learned to live with. We value candidates who have the instinct to spot a "normalized" problem and the AI-native curiosity to create a solution using the latest tools. Our culture is built on iteration, leveraging AI to ship faster today to make it better tomorrow, while ensuring that every improvement, no matter how small, is shared across the team to lift everyone up. If you’re the type of person who values curiosity over bureaucracy, and that AI is a partner in solving tough problems to keep the Internet moving forward, you’ll fit right in. Available Locations: Atlanta, GA; Austin, TX; Denver, CO; Seattle, WA; Washington D.C. About the Role This role focuses on sourcing and onboarding suppliers globally for Data Center services such as data center field services, IT asset disposal services, network provisioning services, logistics support, rack integration support, and service delivery of infrastructure. You will create sourcing plans for each category and quickly deliver these through supplier capability reviews, pre-qualification and onboarding, and master contract negotiations. It is critical that you identify ways to forge partnerships with new suppliers, evaluate suppliers' performance against clearly defined metrics that you will develop or improve together with internal stakeholders, and balance priorities of both Cloudflare and your suppliers to achieve mutually beneficial outcomes. You will continually monitor the effectiveness of these new partnerships and take appropriate actions to ensure ongoing competitive sustainability of our supplier markets for upcoming projects. descriptionAr: Job Title: Patient Care Advocate Job Location: Remote About Us: We are a dedicated team focused on improving access to affordable prescription medications for patients. By partnering with insurance companies, healthcare providers, and pharmacies, we work to reduce the financial burden of medications, ensuring that patients can access the treatments they need without excessive costs. Role Overview: As a key member of our team, you will help patients navigate our Prescription Payment Plan. This involves working closely with patients, insurance providers, healthcare professionals, and pharmacies to ensure seamless enrollment, eligibility verification, cost-sharing, and prescription fulfillment. What You’ll Do: Patient Enrollment & Eligibility : Assist patients with enrolling in the program, ensuring all necessary personal and insurance information is provided and verifying eligibility. Prescription Coverage : Help patients confirm that their prescribed medications are covered under the program, and manage the approval process for eligible medications. Cost-Sharing & Payment : Reduce patients' out-of-pocket costs by applying the program benefits. Manage copayments, coinsurance, and assist with additional copay assistance when applicable. Prescription Fulfillment : Coordinate with participating pharmacies to ensure the correct application of benefits during prescription filling, ensuring patients pay the reduced amount. Refills & Continued Use : Support patients by ensuring they continue receiving medications at reduced costs, monitoring adherence to medication regimens, and ensuring continued eligibility. Program Renewal & Updates : Guide patients through annual renewals and inform them about any updates to the program or medication formulary. What We’re Looking For: High school diploma or GED required Experience in healthcare, insurance or customer service required (experience with prescription assistance programs is a plus) Strong attention to detail and ability to navigate complex processes Excellent communication skills for working with patients, healthcare providers, and pharmacies A genuine passion for helping others and making a positive impact on their healthcare access The ability to work efficiently and collaboratively within a team environment Success Factors for Working from Home Private Workspace: A dedicated, quiet workspace with a door that closes, free from ambient noise. Ergonomics : A comfortable desk and chair setup that allows for the proper installation of necessary equipment. Reliable Internet Connection : Stable, high-speed internet with a minimum bandwidth of 10 Mbps downstream and 5 Mbps upstream. Quiet, Distraction-Free Workspace : A dedicated, quiet area where you can focus on delivering excellent customer service without interruptions. Tech-Savvy : Comfort with technology and ability to learn new systems quickly. Self-motivation & Independence : Ability to stay productive and manage your time effectively in a remote environment. Communication Skills : Strong verbal and written communication skills, especially in a virtual setting. Adaptability : Ability to adapt to changing technologies and procedures while working remotely. Compensation & Perks Hourly Pay : $16.50 per hour Company-Provided Equipment: All necessary equipment will be provided. Comprehensive Benefits : Full health insurance package including medical, dental, and vision coverage. Cell Phone Benefits : $25/month per line for unlimited phone, text, and data (restrictions may apply). Generous Referral Program : Earn $50 per paycheck for every person you refer—and your referral earns it too! No limits on payouts. Comprehensive Training : Paid training to ensure you are fully prepared for success. Career Growth : Opportunities for career advancement and professional development within a leading healthcare provider. Work-from-Home Convenience : Save time, and money, and reduce your environmental footprint. Inclusive Culture : We are an Equal Opportunity Employer, including individuals with disabilities and veterans. What Success Looks Like: Reduced out-of-pocket costs for patients through effective cost-sharing and copay assistance Timely and accurate processing of prescription claims and approvals High patient satisfaction with the program’s support and streamlined experience Compliance with program requirements and monitoring of patient eligibility for ongoing assistance Why Join Us? descriptionAr: About Ramp Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books. The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving. We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome. The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same. If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it. About the Role Ramp's SMB sales team runs a high-velocity, full-cycle sales motion. We sell Ramp's full platform (corporate cards, expense management, bill pay, and procurement) to businesses with up to 150 employees, working with their founders, CEOs, and finance leaders. In this role, you'll help small businesses find a better way to manage their spend and run their finances. You'll own each customer relationship from the first conversation through close: learning how the business operates today, uncovering what's slowing the team down, and showing how Ramp solves it. It's a fast-moving seat with a lot of customer conversations, so you'll sharpen your discovery and closing craft quickly and see your impact in every customer you bring on. This is a role for a seller who has done the work at both ends of the funnel: someone who started their sales career as an SDR, earned a closing seat, and wants a much bigger volume of at-bats. You'll get coaching, a team that shares what works, and clear paths to grow into Commercial sales, Ramp's newer AI product teams, account management, or leadership. What You'll Do Own the full sales cycle for SMB customers, from discovery and demo through pricing, negotiation, and close. Run 10–12 customer conversations a day while keeping a clean, accurate pipeline and forecast. Close at high volume (the team expects 50–60 new customers a month per rep once ramped). Self-source part of your business through daily outbound (about 10% of your closed-won customers). Run focused discovery with founders, CEOs, and finance leaders, and connect Ramp to the pain they describe. Learn Ramp's products and internal tools quickly, and adapt as products and workflows change. What You Need 2–3 years of combined sales experience, including at least one year in a quota-carrying, closing AE role. A start in sales development (SDR or BDR) or another outbound role, with a track record of self-sourcing pipeline. Experience selling SaaS or tech, ideally a product similar to Ramp. A track record as a top performer against quota. Comfort leading pricing and negotiation conversations. Strong organization: you can prioritize a large book of deals and keep each one moving. Comfort with change and ambiguity in a fast-moving, high-intensity environment. Nice to have Experience selling to executive buyers such as CFOs, CEOs, or directors of finance. Familiarity with finance or Office of the CFO topics (we'll coach this). Experience managing a pipeline in Gong or a similar deal board with forecast categories. descriptionAr: About the team OpenAI’s Forward Deployed Engineering team builds with customers to bring frontier AI into production. Our Cyber FDEs partner with the security and engineering teams that defend globally critical systems, from enterprise software to the core infrastructure it runs on. Cyber FDEs work closely with our Product, Research, and Go-to-Market teams to adapt our products and models to what customers need to defend their systems. About the role You’ll build systems that give defenders an advantage at a scale few engineering teams encounter. You might help an enterprise identify, test, and deploy patches across hundreds of thousands of code repositories, or help a security team analyze petabytes of logs for signs of malicious agents or coordinated attacks. Across these deployments, you’ll build tools that customer engineers can trust to support consequential security decisions. You’ll work directly with customer security teams, from CISOs to frontline analysts. As AI changes how attackers operate, you’ll help these teams determine where their defenses need to evolve, prioritize what to build, and validate solutions with the engineers who will operate them. Alongside OpenAI’s account teams, you’ll translate security priorities into deployed systems that help defenders cover more ground. You’ll also help shape what OpenAI builds next. When you identify a gap between what defenders need and what today’s models or products can do, you’ll partner with Research and Product to define, build, and test capabilities that address it. This role is based in New York. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week. We offer relocation assistance. Travel up to 50% is required. In this role you will: Partner with customer security leaders and OpenAI’s Go-to-Market team to scope engagements, establish responsibilities, and define measurable success criteria. Lead technical design and implementation alongside customer engineers. Integrate agents into security workflows, establish access boundaries, and determine which actions require human review. Build evaluations grounded in the decisions defenders make. For a patching agent, test whether a fix blocks a known exploit while preserving expected application behavior. For a detection system, replay historical attacks alongside normal traffic to measure detection speed and false-positive rates. Guide production rollout with the engineers who will operate the system. Provide the observability and controls they need to understand system behavior, intervene when necessary, and expand adoption with confidence. Translate successful approaches across deployments into reusable tools and engineering practices that other defenders can adopt. You might thrive in this role if you: 5+ years of software engineering experience, including building and shipping production software. Experience protecting production systems through work in security engineering, infrastructure, SRE, DevOps, or product engineering. Experience building and evaluating AI agents for software engineering workflows. Experience with CI/CD pipelines and practices that maintain code quality, reliability, and security. Ability to navigate unfamiliar codebases and contribute maintainable, production-quality changes. Ability to communicate technical concepts and trade-offs to engineering teams and senior security stakeholders. Additional experience Cybersecurity spans many disciplines, and while we’re primarily looking for strong engineering generalists, we’d love to hear about deeper experience in any of the following areas: Security curiosity and experimentation: You read CVE write-ups because you want to understand how things break. You may have built an agent honeypot to test a hypothesis—or prove a point—and enjoy turning a security question into a hands-on experiment. Security community engagement: You enjoy exchanging ideas with defenders, whether that’s discussing security strategy with a CISO at Black Hat or comparing technical approaches with frontline practitioners. Application security: You’ve written CodeQL queries or Semgrep rules, built fuzzing harnesses, or discovered and responsibly disclosed vulnerabilities. Automated remediation: CI/CD is your happy place. You’ve built tooling that turns security findings into tested patches, dependency upgrades, or configuration changes across large codebases. Detection engineering: You’ve written and deployed detections using Sigma, YARA, Splunk, or KQL and tested them against attacker behavior. Cloud and identity security: You’ve designed cloud IAM architectures and investigated abuse of workload identities, role hierarchies, or cross-account trust. Security research: You’ve reverse-engineered malware, developed exploit reproductions, or contributed to vulnerability research. Agent security: You’ve tested agents for prompt injection, tool misuse, or credential exposure and built defenses against them.
